q: Replace your tires when the tread is less than how deep?
e: Or when the tread-wear indicators touch the road.
s: Replace tires when the tread is less than 1.5 millimetres deep or when tread-wear indicators touch the road.

q: You sell your car. What happens to the licence plates?
a: You keep them: plates belong to the owner, not the car
w: They stay on the car for the new owner
You mail them to the buyer
e: Ontario uses a plate-to-owner system. Remove your plates when you sell.
s: This means that vehicle licence plates move with the vehicle owner, not the vehicle. When you sell or change vehicles, you must remove your plates.

q: May passengers ride in a house trailer while it's being towed?
a: No: you may not carry anyone in any trailer being towed
w: Yes, in a boat trailer only
e: No passengers in any trailer, including house and boat trailers.
s: You may not carry any person in any trailer, including a house or boat trailer, when it is being towed.

q: How many trailers may you tow behind a regular (non-commercial) vehicle?
w: As many as the hitch can hold
e: It is against the law to tow more than one trailer behind a non-commercial vehicle.
s: It is against the law to tow more than one trailer behind non-commercial vehicles.

q: You're towing a trailer and a big truck passes you. The wind makes your trailer sway. What should you do?
a: Don't brake: steer carefully back into position (a slight increase in speed may help)
w: Pull onto the shoulder at full speed
e: Braking can make the sway worse.
s: When you experience this, do not brake. Carefully steer your vehicle and trailer back into position. A slight increase in speed may help.

q: You're backing up with a trailer and want the trailer to go to the RIGHT. Which way do you steer?
w: It depends on the trailer's weight
e: Backing a trailer is opposite: steer left to back right.
s: To back up to the right, steer to the left.

q: You'll be parked for a few minutes. To save fuel and cut pollution, what should you do?
a: Turn off the engine if you'll be parked for more than 10 seconds
w: Leave it running so it stays warm
Turn it off only if parked over 10 minutes
e: Even in cold weather, engines warm up within 30 seconds.
s: Turn off your vehicle if parked more than 10 seconds.

q: Which of these helps your car use less fuel?
w: Topping off the gas tank every time
Leaving the roof rack on all year
Idling to warm up for 10 minutes
e: Proper tire pressure saves fuel and reduces tire wear and emissions.
s: Keep your tires properly inflated to reduce your fuel bill, emissions and tire wear.

q: Is car insurance required in Ontario?
a: Yes: every vehicle registered in Ontario must be insured
w: Only if you have a loan on the car
e: You must show proof of insurance to register a vehicle or renew its registration.
s: Ontario has compulsory automobile insurance. This means every vehicle registered in the province must be insured.

q: Who can inspect your vehicle and take it off the road if it's unsafe?
a: A police officer or Ministry of Transportation inspector, at any time
w: No one, if your registration is valid
e: It's illegal to drive a vehicle in dangerous condition.
s: A police officer or Ministry of Transportation inspector can examine your vehicle, its equipment and any trailer attached to it, at any time.

q: What is the heaviest trailer you may tow with a G1, G2 or G licence?
e: Heavier trailers may need a higher licence class or a permit. (1,360 kg is when the trailer needs its own brakes.)
s: You must have a valid driver's licence (Class G1, G2 or G) or higher class of licence to tow a trailer with a gross vehicle weight of up to 4,600 kilograms.

q: A trailer (with its load) weighs 1,360 kg or more. What must it have?
a: Brakes strong enough to stop and hold it
w: A licence plate on the front
s: If your trailer has a gross trailer weight, vehicle and load of 1,360 kilograms or more, it must have brakes strong enough to stop and hold the trailer.

q: How must safety chains be attached between a car and trailer?
e: Crossed chains stop the tongue from dropping onto the road if the hitch comes loose.
s: If safety chains are used, they must be crossed under the tongue to prevent the tongue from drop­ping to the road if the primary hitch accidentally disconnects.
